question: Following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, various states sent lists of individuals designated as IS terrorists to Europol with a view to their registration in the Schengen Information System (SIS). As Europol itself is not empowered to enter an alert in the SIS, it must secure the willing cooperation of Member States to do so. 1.

From which authorities in which countries – in particular the US and Israel – did Europol receive lists of persons suspected of terrorism following the fall of the Assad regime, and how many people were on those lists, broken down by the state that sent them?

Through which line of communication were the lists forwarded to the Member States, and did Europol verify the information contained therein or simply forward them to the Member States without verification?
Which EU Member States or Schengen countries actually entered such alerts, and how many were entered per country?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.7.2026) The Commission has asked the European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation (Europol) to provide a response to the question raised by the Honourable Member. The Commission will send the Agency’s reply to the Honourable Member as soon as possible.
